Apple further disclosed details about the Apple Music AI labeling requirements it had previously announced back in March, as detailed below.

AI-generated content will be clearly labeled on Apple Music

Earlier this year, Apple announced that Apple Music would require AI transparency disclosures for cover art, songs, compositions, and music videos submitted to the platform.

Now, Apple has shared further execution details for this initiative.

In an email sent to creators today, Apple stated: "Later this year, we will also surface these markers to Apple Music listeners in the form of a 'Made With AI' label."

Apple has also clarified exactly when disclosures are required. The email reads as follows:

Apple Music added that the goal of this initiative is "to provide as much transparency as possible to listeners" and asked creators to refer to their Style Guide for more details.

Apple Music's approach is just the latest example of streaming platforms grappling with the influx of AI-generated music, as more and more artists incorporate generative AI into their creative workflows.

Spotify previously stated that it would, by default, exclude music from AI personas from its editorial and algorithmic recommendations; Deezer announced last year that it would exclude fully AI-generated tracks from its recommendations and editorial playlists. Deezer also disclosed last month that fully AI-generated music accounted for more than 50% of all newly uploaded songs on the platform for the first time.

As for Apple Music, the platform's lead Oliver Schusser revealed during a recent appearance on Billboard's On the Record podcast that although more than one-third of the music uploaded to Apple Music each month is fully AI-generated, it accounts for less than 0.5% of plays on the service.
